title: TAEIR: Trust-Aware Edge Intelligence for Proactive ICU Risk Management
content: Intensive-care monitoring remains dominated by single-parameter threshold alarms, of which the large majority are non-actionable and which contribute to alarm fatigue and delayed response. Machine-learning early-warning systems trained on retrospective ICU databases have demonstrated strong discrimination for sepsis and circulatory failure, yet independent evaluations of widely deployed proprietary models show that discrimination in one cohort does not translate into calibrated, trustworthy alerts in another. Existing edge/IoT ICU architectures, meanwhile, treat inference as a classification problem and rarely address predictive uncertainty, calibration, explanation, drift, or the governance mechanisms clinicians need in order to trust an alert. Building on the authors' earlier IoT/Edge-AI Smart ICU Monitoring System [1], which established edge-deployed predictive monitoring but did not address uncertainty, calibration, explanation, alarm policy or assurance, this paper proposes TAEIR (Trust-Aware Edge Intelligence for ICU Risk), a nine-layer framework in which (i) multimodal physiological streams (ECG-derived features, SpO₂/PPG, arterial and non-invasive blood pressure, respiration, temperature and sparse laboratory values) are quality-scored, synchronised and encoded by a lightweight temporal architecture suitable for edge inference; (ii) deterioration risk is estimated together with decomposed predictive uncertainty and post-hoc calibration, with a formal abstention rule; (iii) a Dynamic Clinical Risk Score (DCRS) combines calibrated probability, uncertainty, trajectory, persistence, severity, signal quality and patient context into an alarm-prioritisation policy that replaces fixed thresholds; (iv) explanations are generated at the level of which signals changed, over which window, and how much each contributed; and (v) an explicit AI assurance layer monitors calibration, drift, data quality, fairness and human-override behaviour, and enforces fail-safe fallback to conventional monitoring. We formalise the framework mathematically, specify an edge–cloud partitioning policy, and design a reproducible multi-database experimental protocol on MIMIC-IV, eICU-CRD, HiRID and the PhysioNet/CinC 2019 sepsis challenge data, with an explicit primary-task/secondary-task hierarchy, patient-level temporally ordered splits, clinically oriented metrics (sensitivity at fixed false-alarm rates, lead time, false alarms per patient-day, ECE, Brier score, selective-prediction risk–coverage) and a full ablation plan. This is a framework, methodology and benchmark-design paper: it establishes the architecture, the mathematical formulation, the uncertainty–calibration–conformal machinery, the risk policy, the assurance architecture and a pre-registered protocol, and it reports no experimental results, hardware measurements or clinical outcomes. The system is positioned strictly as clinician-in-the-loop decision support.
